text: Spot on. This is also why I believe there is a rise in personality disorders. So many people tend to create a false personality in order to adapt to dysfunctional family dynamics, just to get along. That comes with denying your core self, so they end up not even knowing who they are as a person, because the true self has been forbidden to exist. That leaves nothing but anger and usually at the core is a fear of abandonment after being told expressing the real you isn't an option. You're taught you have to work/perform well for people to love you. And then that translates into relationships being unsafe, so you have to work for love having been taught that no one will love you just for who you are. And any criticism of who you are then triggers that anger so you put your hands on anyone who insults you.... because you can't do that to the real people who hurt you, which is usually the family. It's a vicious cycle that blocks the development of healthy coping skills that lead to emotional maturity. It's a mess that I see all around me, especially with the younger generations.

After the second time, the police understood the situation and warned us that there had been an increase in assaults in Korea for this type of issue so we have to be careful. People have been attacking their neighbors because they think they are too loud. 
I have so many other stories.

You make some really good points that are actually addressed in a lot of countries ( or at least tried to be the focus), my degree in criminology really opened my eyes to the complexity of this, it’s way more nuanced than people realise. Your point where you talk about society giving up on people relates to the labelling theory by Lombroso (not to be mistaken with Lombrozo, he had a more damaging viewpoint imo with his “born criminal” theories). The labelling theory is a huge concern when it comes to youth crime as well because if everyone treats a child (or anyone) like they’re a waste of space, have no value etc, eventually they will just end up living that as their reality and lean into it. Humans need worth and value to have something to strive for, some of the first steps of rehabilitation is giving people skills and encouragement. 
I could go on forever, but I really liked that you made this video, it would be good if governments could make moves to help society grow, and it really does often go back to basics like learning how to process emotions and know one’s worth.
Unfortunately, many people never learn emotion regulation.
